metadata.title: PISA for development technical strand c (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD Strand C paper is a methodology and technical guidance document for incorporating out-of-school 15-year-olds into PISA for Development; it does not report an implemented student-level analytic dataset with an estimated outcome model. The document discusses how a sampling frame could be constructed (e.g., two-stage household listing and revisits; or targeted area sampling using poverty maps) and how probability sampling would require design-effect considerations for clustered sampling points. It also notes that household surveys can under-represent marginalised groups and that adjustments may be needed when estimating the size/location of groups missing from sampling frames. Because no final analytic microdata analysis is presented, no specific PISA-style student weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is applied or named in the paper.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this document does not estimate cognitive achievement PV-based outcomes for students; instead, it provides technical issues and recommended procedures for counting, locating, sampling, administering interviews/tests, and designing instruments for out-of-school 15-year-olds. Similarly, missing-data handling is not reported because there is no empirical model estimation on a student-level dataset with an analytic sample and missingness mechanism. The paper is therefore a framework/methodology design exercise rather than an analysis paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic student sample is constructed in this paper. It provides methodological guidance for Strand C, including recommended sampling approaches (two-stage listing and revisits; targeted area sampling using poverty maps; possible supplementary frames for pastoralist groups; and separate sampling for non-household populations such as street children and institutions). It also reports descriptive estimates from external sources (e.g., DHS/MICS/administrative data) and discusses how Strand C instruments would be administered and linked to PISA scales, but it does not specify inclusion/exclusion rules for a final analytic dataset.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD technical strand paper (Strand C) addresses how PISA for Development could assess out-of-school 15-year-olds, focusing on definitional issues (what counts as out-of-school), counting and locating the target group, constructing sampling frames, and designing inclusive instruments and contextual questionnaires. It recommends a two-stage approach: first identify households reporting a 15-year-old, then revisit to verify age and schooling status and administer a filter, test, and contextual questionnaire. For sampling, it discusses probability sampling (with large household listing requirements) versus targeted sampling of marginal/vulnerable areas using poverty maps, and it highlights challenges in under-coverage of marginalised groups in standard household surveys. For measurement, it proposes a modular set of cognitive assessments (from PISA booklets to ASER/Uwezo-like basic literacy/numeracy and pictorial/verbal tasks) with filters to route respondents to appropriate difficulty levels, and it outlines linking strategies using Rasch/IRT models. The paper does not provide predictive ML results or PV-based achievement estimates; its contribution is methodological guidance for future implementation and instrument development.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a methodology/technical guidance document rather than an empirical ML study: it does not report a student-level analytic sample, PV-based outcomes, missing-data handling for an estimation model, or any trained ML algorithm with performance metrics. Consequently, fields such as total_students, per-country n_students for an analytic dataset, plausible-value handling for achievement modeling, and main_findings (structured ML results) are not applicable to the paper’s purpose.
